title: Benchmark Ground_Truth
description: One benchmark case's expected review outcome. Written from the defects deliberately placed in the case template, before any review is run, and never derived from review output. benchmark/README.md states the methodology rules; benchmark/harness/metrics.py consumes the fields defined here.

schema_version.description: Version of this Ground_Truth format, independent of the plugin version and of the Review_Report schema_version. Bumped per semver when a field is added, removed, or changes meaning.

case_id.description: Identifier of the case, equal to the name of the directory holding this file. 001-099 are defect cases, 101-199 are clean cases used as negative tests.

template.description: Reviewed template, as a file name relative to the case directory. No path separators: a Ground_Truth file describes its own directory and nothing outside it.

description.description: What the template contains and which defects were placed in it, in prose. Read by a human deciding whether the expected findings below are the right expectations.

authored_before_review.description: Declaration that these expectations were written before the review pipeline was run against the template. Always true: a case whose expectations were reverse-engineered from review output measures nothing, so there is no legal way to record that state. The declaration is not machine-verifiable; CI checks it indirectly by requiring ground_truth.json to appear in the same commit as template.yaml or earlier.

expected_finding_count.description: Number of entries in expected_findings. Counted at the report's granularity: one finding per resource per Normalized_Category (see benchmark/README.md). Stated redundantly so that an expectation dropped by a careless edit is visible; tests assert the two agree.

expected_findings.description: Findings the review is expected to report for this template. Order is significant only for tie-breaking: when two entries share a match key, the harness consumes actual findings in the order written here.

expected_findings_agent_only.description: Reserved for a future benchmark mode in which agent findings are the subject of measurement rather than a fixed fixture. Required, and empty in v0.1, so that adding the mode does not change this format. No maxItems constraint is imposed, so a future mode can populate it without a schema change.

expected_findings_human_review.description: Reserved for a future benchmark mode measuring findings only a human reviewer is expected to reach. Required, and empty in v0.1, so that adding the mode does not change this format. No maxItems constraint is imposed, so a future mode can populate it without a schema change.

expectedFinding.description: One expected finding, at the report's granularity: one resource, one Normalized_Category. Several distinct problems of the same category on the same resource are one entry, because the report merges them into one finding.

resource.description: Logical ID of the resource the finding is about, or null for a template-level finding. Part of the match key; null compares as the empty string.

normalized_category.description: Expected Finding.Normalized_Category. Part of the match key. The closed set is the categories array of iacreview/category_map.json.

finding_type.description: Expected Finding.FindingType. Part of the match key.

severity.description: Expected Finding.Severity. Deliberately not part of the match key: a severity mismatch is measured as Severity Accuracy, so that it does not also count as a missed detection.

confidence.description: Expected Finding.Confidence, when the case means to pin it. Optional: it follows from detection_class unless stated (deterministic implies Confirmed, agent-dependent implies Likely, the strongest confidence an agent finding may carry). Together with finding_type this expresses the four finding classes the security policy distinguishes: a confirmed issue is Confirmed, a likely risk is Likely, a contextual recommendation is Contextual, and an informational note is finding_type Informational.

detection_class.description: Whether reaching this finding requires agent reasoning. deterministic findings are held to a 100% detection rate; agent-dependent findings are measured and reported without a pass/fail threshold.

detected_by.description: Sources expected to report this finding. Used to filter expectations when the harness runs a single-Source mode; a finding several Sources reach lists all of them.

note.description: Which defect in the template this entry stands for, in prose. Not compared against Finding text: matching is by resource, FindingType and Normalized_Category, never by description string equality.

normalizedCategory.description: Closed Normalized_Category set. Kept identical to the categories array of iacreview/category_map.json; a test fails if the two drift apart.

findingType.description: Permitted FindingType values, as defined by iacreview.finding.FINDING_TYPES.

severity.description: Permitted Severity values, as defined by iacreview.finding.SEVERITIES. Severity is comparable only among findings sharing a FindingType.

confidence.description: Permitted Confidence values, as defined by iacreview.finding.CONFIDENCES.

source.description: Permitted Source values, as defined by iacreview.finding.SOURCES.
